chunks.text: Welcome to the Slow English podcast.
In this podcast, we speak slow and easy English.
Today we talk about a very unusual city.
The city is Yakutsk.
Yakutsk is in Russia.
It is in the eastern part of the country.
The city is in a region called Siberia.
Yakutsk is famous because it is one of the coldest cities in the world.
Yakutsk is located near the Lena River.
The Lena River is one of the longest rivers in the world.
The city is very far from many other large cities.
Because of this, life there can feel remote and quiet.
The winter in Yakutsk is extremely cold.
Temperatures can fall to minus 40 degrees Celsius or even colder.
People wear very warm clothes like thick coats, fur hats, and boots.
Life continues even in the very cold weather.
Part 4.
Because the ground is always frozen, buildings in Yakutsk are built in a special way.
The ground is called permafrost.
Buildings stand on tall supports above the ground.
This helps protect the buildings from the frozen earth.
Part 5.
The people in Yakutsk are strong and used to the cold climate.
Many people belong to the Yakut or Saka ethnic group.
They have their own language and traditions.
Culture and traditions are very important in this region.
Part 6.
One interesting place in Yakutsk is the Mammoth Museum.
In Siberia, scientists sometimes find frozen mammoths in the ice.
Mammoths were large animals that lived thousands of years ago.
The museum shows fossils and information about these ancient animals.
Part 7.
Another unique place is the permafrost kingdom.
It is a museum built inside ice caves.
Inside the caves, everything is made of ice.
Visitors can see ice sculptures and frozen walls.
Part 8.
Even though the winters are very cold, summers in Yakutsk can be warm.
In summer temperatures can reach 25 degrees Celsius.
The city becomes green and full of life.
People enjoy parks, rivers, and outdoor activities.
Part 9.
Food in Yakutsk is influenced by the cold climate.
People often eat meat and fish.
One traditional food is frozen fish cut into thin slices.
This dish is called stroganina.
It is eaten while still frozen.
Part 10.
Yakutsk also has theaters, schools, and universities.
Young people study and work just like in other cities.
The city continues to grow and develop.
Modern life and traditional culture exist together.
Part 11.
The Lena River is very important for transportation.
In summer boats travel on the river.
In winter the river freezes and sometimes people travel across the ice.
Nature strongly influences daily life in the city.
Part 12.
Yakutsk is a city of extremes.
The cold winters, the frozen ground, and the unique culture make it very special.
Even though it is far away and very cold, Yakutsk is an interesting and fascinating place.
